campaign: safe-c33 shared-contract establishment (E2 follow-on: the X509_VERIFY_POLICY extension-method v2i config decoders)
subphase: B51 takes the 10 v2i config-decoder sites left BLOCKED by B50. Unlike the i2s/i2r print path, v2i is dispatched by do_ext_nconf (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:998-1107), not X509V3_EXT_print. B51 contracts the 10 callbacks and B51b adds the registry read hold across the config-decode slots: RegistryReadGuard spans do_ext_nconf's lookup-through-callback-and-encode span (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1035), X509V3_EXT_i2d's encoder (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:742) and X509V3_EXT_d2i's decoder (src/x509/v3_lib.rs:892). Row liveness for a DYNAMIC row is therefore enforced rather than a caller duty. The measured source delta 3d32259e6..8b9a03e28 is 748 insertions / 18 deletions across 12 files, not additive: it also fixes (B51-R3) the `strspn` offset narrowing in v2i_ASIdentifiers and (B51-R4) the asid push-failure double release, with a discriminating free-probe test for R4. The discharge is NOT applied: CAMPAIGN-STATUS.json is untouched and the closure was not run.

authority.note: The authority builds STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE) from X509V3_parse_list(value) or NCONF_get_section(conf, value + 1), refuses NULL or empty, calls the first of v2i/s2i/r2i that is set, encodes the result through method->it or method->i2d, then frees it with method->ext_free or ASN1_item_free. The candidate's do_ext_nconf is the same shape; it adds no refusal the authority lacks except the guards recorded here. The brief's stated v2i signature (method, unsigned char **, long) and ext_free release belong to the d2i/print path, not to v2i; the actual slot is (method, X509V3_CTX *, STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE) *) and all ten rows release through `it` with ext_free NULL. That discrepancy is recorded in B51-R7 and is not silently repaired.

shared_contract: v2i slot contract stated on X509V3ExtMethod (src/x509/v3_lib.rs). do_ext_nconf holds RegistryReadGuard across the whole dispatch (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1035), so the row resolved through X509V3_EXT_get_nid stays live across the lookup, the v2i callback and the encoder; it refuses ext_nid == NID_undef (:1007), a NULL row (:1014), and a NULL or empty value stack (:1041); it builds STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE) from X509V3_parse_list (own, freed at :1060-1063) or NCONF_get_section (section-owned, not freed); it calls cb(method, ctx, nval) at :1059; on a non-NULL result it encodes through do_ext_i2d at :1098 and releases with ASN1_item_free(ext_struc, it()) at :1099-1101. The callback must consume `nval` read-only, must not free/retain it or its members, must not retain `method`/`ctx`, and must return a fresh object of exactly the row's `it` type, releasing any partial value itself on failure.

entry_points: X509V3_EXT_nconf_nid (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1212) -> do_ext_nconf(:998); this is the entry the three tests drive.
X509V3_EXT_conf (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1426) and X509V3_EXT_conf_nid (:1455) build a temporary NCONF and call the two above.
X509V3_EXT_add_nconf_sk (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1245) walks a config section and calls X509V3_EXT_nconf_int(:1291).
dispatch_paths.lookup: X509V3_EXT_get_nid (src/x509/v3_lib.rs:748) takes a registry read hold for the lookup only and returns a BORROWED row (documented at :740-746). do_ext_nconf takes its own RegistryReadGuard at :1035 and holds it across the v2i/s2i/r2i slot read, the callback and do_ext_i2d, so a concurrent X509V3_EXT_cleanup cannot release the row for the whole dispatch. The lookup's short hold nests as a second read on the same thread.
dispatch_paths.values: at_section = (*value == '@') (:1031); X509V3_parse_list(value) (:1037) is an owning list the dispatcher frees after the call (:1060-1063); NCONF_get_section(conf, value + 1) (:1034) is a section-owned stack it must not free.
dispatch_paths.guard: nval.is_null() || OPENSSL_sk_num(nval) <= 0 is refused at :1041-1057 before any callback; this is the pre-slot guard the callback contracts rely on (B51-C1).
dispatch_paths.encode: do_ext_i2d(method, ext_nid, crit, ext_struc) at :1098; it uses method->it when set (:614-633) else method->i2d (:634-647).
dispatch_paths.free: ASN1_item_free(ext_struc, it()) at :1099-1101 when `it` is set; method->ext_free at :1102-1104 when it is not. All ten rows set `it` and ext_free is None.
dispatch_paths.lifetime: `method` is borrowed from X509V3_EXT_get_nid and is protected by do_ext_nconf's RegistryReadGuard (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1035) across the callback and encoder; the caller is not required to exclude X509V3_EXT_cleanup for the duration of the call. The hold ends at dispatch return and does not extend caller-owned row storage (X509V3_EXT_add's own Safety). `nval` is live across the call and is freed only after it when the dispatcher owns it; `ext_struc` is exclusively the dispatcher's from the callback return to :1098/:1101. The callback retains neither `method`, `nval`, nor its members.
dispatch_paths.allocator: ext_struc is a fresh value from the row's item allocator on the CRYPTO_* seam; the DER block is CRYPTO_malloc'd by ASN1_item_i2d and owned by do_ext_i2d's OwnedBuf (drop site :184). The dispatch itself allocates nothing beyond the parse list.
dispatch_paths.second_reader: The only production reads of a v2i slot are do_ext_nconf's :1020-1028. No test or other unit reads a v2i slot.
dispatch_paths.ctx: ctx is NULL or a live X509V3_CTX; do_ext_nconf does not check it. Only v2i_AUTHORITY_INFO_ACCESS forwards it (to v2i_GENERAL_NAME_ex, which documents NULL-or-live); the other nine ignore it.
dispatch_paths.retention: The callback may retain nothing. Its non-NULL result transfers to the dispatcher, which encodes it and releases it exactly once; a NULL result is reported as a failed extension build.

row_liveness.question: Does the registry read hold span the v2i dispatch, as it spans the i2s/i2r print path?
row_liveness.answer: YES, ENFORCED. B49/B50 relied on a hold in X509V3_EXT_print; the config-decode path had none, because X509V3_EXT_get_nid takes and releases the read lock at return. B51b adds RegistryReadGuard over the whole lookup-through-slot span in do_ext_nconf, X509V3_EXT_i2d and X509V3_EXT_d2i, so a concurrent X509V3_EXT_cleanup cannot release a DYNAMIC row under the callback. The duty is no longer documentary.
row_liveness.enforcement: src/x509/v3_conf.rs do_ext_nconf (~:1035), X509V3_EXT_i2d (~:742); src/x509/v3_lib.rs X509V3_EXT_d2i (~:892). RAII: RegistryReadGuard::Drop unlocks on every path, including early NULL returns.
row_liveness.observation: A #[cfg(test)] thread-local probe (v3_lib.rs read_hold_probe) is incremented by RegistryReadGuard::acquire and decremented by Drop; registry_read_held_on_this_thread() is absent from non-test builds and adds no exported item. A neutral control asserts the probe is false before dispatch, so true readings are not vacuous.
row_liveness.static_rows: The ten rows are process-lifetime pub static values reached through STANDARD_EXTS; X509V3_EXT_cleanup cannot release them.
row_liveness.dynamic_rows: X509V3_EXT_add_alias can copy a row containing a v2i slot into a DYNAMIC allocation released by ext_list_free; the added read hold now excludes that release for the whole dispatch.
row_liveness.caller_rows: X509V3_EXT_add still accepts a caller-owned row and the list borrows it (only DYNAMIC rows are freed). Caller storage lifetime stays a stated caller obligation on X509V3_EXT_add's own # Safety block; the registry lock does not and cannot protect the caller memory. A callback registered by a caller must also not re-enter a registry writer (B51-R9).

defect_class: uncontracted unsafe fn definitions at 10 X509_VERIFY_POLICY v2i sites. The blocks already carried per-line SAFETY comments but no fn-level # Safety. The dispatcher evidence is unchanged (name non-NULL from both producers, value NULL-or-NUL-terminated, NULL-safe stack/parse helpers, correct partial frees). The delta is not additive: besides the ten contracts and three end-to-end tests it adds the registry read hold (B51b) and fixes two functional defects in v2i_ASIdentifiers -- the `strspn` offset narrowing (B51-R3) and the failed-push double release (B51-R4).

boundaries.contract: v2i slot contract on X509V3ExtMethod. Caller do_ext_nconf's v2i arm (:1029-1066) establishes: method is a live borrowed row; nval is a live non-empty stack of live CONF_VALUE elements with non-NULL NUL-terminated name and NULL-or-NUL-terminated value; ctx is NULL or live. The body ignores ctx/method, reads name unconditionally, null-checks value, and canonizes the result. On success it returns a fresh ASIdentifiers owned by the dispatcher, encoded with ASIdentifiers_it and freed once with ASN1_item_free; on failure it frees the partial value. The returned type must match the row's `it` (registrar obligation). Row liveness while the callback runs is enforced by the dispatcher's registry read hold (B51-R1; canary B51-H1), so the caller need not exclude `X509V3_EXT_cleanup` during the call. `X509V3_EXT_add` still borrows caller-owned row storage, the `it`/`usr_data` pairing is the registrar's obligation, and a callback must not call a registry writer (B51-R9).

hidden_obligations_note: No obligation is hidden. Every duty the callbacks do not enforce is stated in each contract and enumerated as a residual: (1) a callback supplied by a caller-registered row must not call a registry writer, because the read hold is non-reentrant (B51-R9); (2) caller-owned row storage must outlive registration (X509V3_EXT_add's own Safety block); (3) the returned object's type must match the row's `it` and the meaning of its `usr_data` (B51-R6); (4) `ctx` is NULL-or-live where the callback reads it (B51-R8). Row liveness for a DYNAMIC row is not an obligation: it is enforced (B51-R1). A hidden obligation is one that is neither enforced nor stated; none was found.
new_unsafe_assumptions_note: B51b adds the RegistryReadGuard abstraction; its unsafe work is the crate's audited CRYPTO_THREAD_read_lock seam, not a new obligation on callers. The ten contracts and three tests add no unsafe fn and no exported item. This correction's source delta is documentation only.
boundary_size: 10 callback bodies (unchanged), 10 fn-level # Safety contracts, one shared dispatcher arm (do_ext_nconf v2i branch, src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1029-1066), and 3 tests (two loops over all ten rows plus one pre-slot canary). The B51b hold is the single shared mechanism; no second lock type or additional hold was added. B51b adds one structural hold mechanism (registry read guard on the config/i2d/d2i paths) shared by all ten sites, with three mutation-proven liveness canaries and one neutral control.
safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: Every entry point that can reach a v2i callback is `unsafe extern "C"` (X509V3_EXT_nconf, X509V3_EXT_nconf_nid, X509V3_EXT_conf, X509V3_EXT_conf_nid, X509V3_EXT_add_nconf_sk). The callback type is Option<unsafe extern "C" fn>, and no safe Rust item accepts or returns X509V3ExtMethod. A safe Rust caller can therefore not reach these callbacks without an unsafe block; the C ABI obligations are stated in each contract.

residuals.description: The closure names 11 BLOCKED v2i-named obligations but B50's taxonomy counts v2i as 10 because bitst_v2i is grouped with bitst_i2v under family bitst. B51 follows the 10-site family and leaves bitst_v2i BLOCKED. Separately, v2i_TLS_FEATURE's owning boundary is recorded ELIMINATED at src/x509/v3_tlsf.rs:146 while the source at :232 was still an uncontracted unsafe fn before this delta; B51 contracts it and records the inconsistency rather than silently reclassifying it.

v2i_ASIdentifiers used to narrow each `strspn` result to `c_int` before using it as a `usize` offset into the NUL-terminated value; a digit/space run longer than INT_MAX would wrap negative. 8b9a03e28 removed the six `as c_int` casts and keeps every offset `usize` (src/x509/v3_asid.rs:1553-1583). Verified with `git diff 3d32259e6 8b9a03e28 -- src/x509/v3_asid.rs`: the removed `as c_int` lines and the `usize` arithmetic are the whole change. No discriminating test is possible: reaching the old wrap needs a single NUL-terminated config value with a run longer than INT_MAX, i.e. a multi-gigabyte input. The fix is a type/flow correction (strspn returns usize; pointer::add takes usize) enforced at compile time, so there is no smaller behaviour to assert.

X509v3_asid_add_id_or_range installed min/max into a fresh ASIdOrRange before OPENSSL_sk_push; on a failed push ASIdOrRange_free released them and v2i_ASIdentifiers' cleanup released them again. 8b9a03e28 detaches both pointers (the range's min/max, or the plain-id choice pointer) before ASIdOrRange_free on that arm (src/x509/v3_asid.rs:1060-1079), so the caller keeps exactly the ownership the contract promises. Verified with `git diff 3d32259e6 8b9a03e28 -- src/x509/v3_asid.rs` and by the discriminating test below, which injects the push failure through the test-only insert fault.
residuals.closed_by: 8b9a03e28; test x509::v3_asid::tests::a_failed_push_returns_the_caller_integers_instead_of_releasing_them (free_probe count 0 before the caller frees, 1 after) recorded and run (B51-REJ-2)

residuals.description: Partial-decode ownership is exercised by v2i_callbacks_reject_bad_values but not proven leak-free: no allocator-hook or LeakSanitizer run was made, so a missing release in a failure path would not be detected.

The dispatcher encodes and frees the returned object with the row's `it` (ASN1_item_i2d / ASN1_item_free; all ten rows set `it` and ext_free is NULL). The callback must return exactly the item's type; a registrar that pairs a v2i callback with a mismatched `it` causes an invalid encode/free. That pairing is not checked by X509V3_EXT_add and is the registrar's obligation.

The subphase brief described v2i as `(X509V3_EXT_METHOD*, unsigned char**, long)` returning `*mut c_void` freed through `ext_free`, and pointed at X509V3_EXT_print. The actual v2i slot is `(const X509V3_EXT_METHOD*, X509V3_CTX*, STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE)*)`, dispatched by do_ext_nconf (v3_conf.c:79-135), and all ten rows are freed through `it` with ASN1_item_free, not ext_free. This receipt follows the code and the closure's v2i items; the brief's signature/release description is recorded here rather than silently adopted.

ctx may be NULL (do_ext_nconf's contract allows it and does not check it). Only v2i_AUTHORITY_INFO_ACCESS forwards ctx, to v2i_GENERAL_NAME_ex, which documents NULL-or-live; the other nine ignore it. A callback that begins reading ctx would inherit the caller's obligation to supply one.

The enforced registry read hold is non-reentrant for writers. src/runtime/thread.rs: LockState { writer, writer_id: Option<CryptoThreadId>, readers } (:177-181); write_lock (:437-447) loops while `writer || readers > 0` and detects re-entry only with `writer_id == Some(me)`; read_lock (:404-411) only increments `readers` and never sets `writer_id`, so a read-holding thread has `writer_id == None`. A callback invoked under the B51b hold -- the v2i branch, and equally the s2i (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1095) and r2i (:1101) branches of the same do_ext_nconf guard -- that calls a registry writer (X509V3_EXT_add, X509V3_EXT_add_list, X509V3_EXT_add_alias, X509V3_EXT_cleanup) therefore self-deadlocks: it waits for its own read count to drop, which cannot happen. Reachability: none of the ten standard rows' callbacks calls a registry writer, so the built-in table cannot trigger it; a caller-registered row's v2i/i2d/d2i can (X509V3_EXT_add registers caller code). Recorded as a named ABI obligation on the registrar/caller: a callback that may run under the registry read hold must not call a registry writer. No deadlocking test is written; the obligation is stated in the ten contracts and here.
residuals.scope_note: The same do_ext_nconf guard also spans the s2i and r2i branches, so R9 applies to all three slot families dispatched there.

The ten boundary contracts still state that a concurrent X509V3_EXT_cleanup must not run during the call (B51-R1), which contradicts marking R1 CLOSED-STRUCTURALLY.
The delta description is false: the measured change is 748 insertions / 18 deletions, including two functional fixes, not "348 insertions, 0 deletions / additive only / no functional defect fixed".
